rule.title: Visa Fraud Monitoring Program
rule.note: This reason code generally cannot be represented. Recommend accepting liability unless the merchant can prove the transaction was miscoded by the issuer.

summary.allegation: The issuer has raised the transaction under the Visa Fraud Monitoring Program, meaning this card account was flagged as fraudulent through Visa's fraud monitoring reporting rather than through a standard dispute.
summary.to_defend: The only defence is documentary proof that the issuer miscoded the dispute under the Visa Fraud Monitoring Program.

requirements.title: Proof the issuer miscoded the chargeback
requirements.text: Evidence that the transaction was miscoded by the issuer under the Visa Fraud Monitoring Program.
requirements.finding: Nothing in the file addresses the coding of the dispute; the merchant supplied a Visa Secure authentication record and a delivery confirmation, both of which speak to transaction validity rather than to whether the issuer applied the wrong reason code.
requirements.gap: No issuer correspondence, Visa case record or fraud reporting extract showing the dispute was raised under the wrong reason code.

documents.label: Visa Secure authentication record
documents.reason: Shows the cardholder was authenticated via 3DS, which evidences a genuine transaction but does not show the issuer miscoded the dispute under the Fraud Monitoring Program.

documents.label: Evri delivery confirmation, order BB-77231
documents.reason: Confirms delivery to the billing postcode, which goes to transaction validity, not to whether the reason code was applied in error.

alerts.text: Visa 10.5 generally cannot be represented. The evidence is shown but does not change the outcome unless it proves miscoding.

reasons: Every requirement the decision relies on is backed by verified evidence

justification: Reason code 10.5 cannot be represented on the merits and no evidence suggests the issuer miscoded the dispute.
rationale:
The issuer has processed this £78.50 transaction of 30 April 2025 (txn_1178ST) under Visa reason code 10.5, Visa Fraud Monitoring Program.
The only defence available under this code is proof that the issuer applied the wrong reason code, and no issuer correspondence or Visa case record addressing coding has been supplied.
The Visa Secure record (ECI 05, authenticated at 2025-04-30 22:14:51 UTC) and the Evri delivery to 22 Cavendish Court, SW4 7QR on 2 May 2025 show the transaction was genuine, but evidence of a genuine transaction does not establish miscoding.
Strong authentication and matching AVS and CVV results are worth raising separately with the acquirer if the account has been flagged in error, but they do not support a representment here.
We recommend accepting liability for the full £78.50.
